summary: Philosopher Giovanni Gentile studied at Scuola Normale Superiore and the University of Florence. He taught at the universities of Palermo, Pisa, and Rome, Scuola Normale Superiore, Bocconi University, and served as president of the Istituto Italiano per il Medio ed Estremo Oriente.

Giovanni Vacca was a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology who studied at the University of Genoa. He held academic posts at the University of Florence (circa 1911–1921) and Sapienza University of Rome (circa 1921–1947).

Giovanni Verardi is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Allahabad, Banaras Hindu University, and Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, and held a post at Kyoto University.

Girindrasekhar Bose worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at Presidency University, Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta, where he later served as Professor of Experimental Psychology from 1917 to 1949.
Gisho Nakano was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held positions at Koyasan University and Kyushu University (circa 1928–1955).
Giuliana Martini is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. In 2010, she held posts at the Italian School of East Asian Studies and Kyoto University.

Giuseppe Bardelli was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien. He served as a lecturer in Coptic and Sanskrit at the University of Pisa from circa 1845 to 1865.
Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti was a linguist who studied at the University of Bologna from circa 1786 to 1797. He subsequently held a post there from circa 1797 to 1831.

Giuseppe Tucci was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Sapienza University of Rome, University of Calcutta, and Visva-Bharati University. He held posts at the University of Calcutta, Sapienza, and ISMEO.

Giuseppe Vignato works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He was a doctoral student at Peking University, studying under Angela Falco Howard, Chongfeng Li, Su Bai, and Shichang Ma, and held a post at Peking University attested in 2017.

Buddhist studies scholar Giyu Nishi studied at the University of Tokyo under Taiken Kimura, Hakuju Ui, Sylvain Lévi, Junjirō Takakusu, Masaharu Anesaki, and Makoto Nagai. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1926) and Toyo University (1927).
Gnanawimala Chandima is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under the instruction of Uma Shankar Vyas.
Godabarish Mishra was an Indologist and philosopher. After studying at Ravenshaw College and the University of Calcutta, he served as Lecturer in Sanskrit and Director at the University of Madras.

Gombojab Tsybikov was a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Tomsk State University and Saint Petersburg State University, and later served as Lecturer of the Mongolian Language at Far Eastern Federal University (circa 1902–1917).

Gopinath Kaviraj worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Allahabad (circa 1910–1914) and served as Professor of Tantra-Śāstra at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1967).

Gordon D. Kaufman worked in religious studies and philosophy. He completed his studies at Northwestern University and Yale Divinity School, and later held a post at Harvard University from circa 1963 to 1996.
Gordon Johnson is a historian and Indologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge from circa 1961 to 1967. He held a post at the University of Cambridge attested in 2012.
Gottfried Hermann was a linguist who studied at Leipzig University and the University of Jena. He subsequently held an academic post at Leipzig University from circa 1798 until 1848.

Sinologist and historian Gottlieb Siegfried Bayer studied at the University of Königsberg under Christoph Theodosius Walther. He held posts at the University of Königsberg, Kathedralschule zu Königsberg, and the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at King's College London in 1858, held a post there in 1861, and later held a post at the Oriental Institute, Woking, from circa 1889 to 1899.
